subject: Learning Methods
title: Linking New Notes to Old Ones
description: A quick win: understand Linking New Notes to Old Ones.

hook.text: A chemistry note from September connected to a biology note from October.

buildup.text: When reviewing new notes, actively look for connections to existing notes from different topics or time periods.

discovery.text: Cross-linking builds a knowledge web. The more connections an idea has, the easier it is to retrieve and apply.

twist.text: The most valuable connections are between distant subjects. Close connections are obvious.

climax.text: During every review session, ask: what else does this connect to? Scan old notes for at least one surprising link.

punchline.text: New note, old link. Cross-connections spark the best insights.

quiz.question: Why are connections between distant subjects particularly valuable?
options: They are easier for the brain to remember
Distant connections produce creative insights that close ones do not
Professors give extra credit for cross-subject references
